B: Only the ears rise above the head.
context: A deer is a hoofed animal with a long face.
coding: Use B when the head is clear and has no visible antler, U when its top cannot be seen.

A: The crown of leaves is longer than the fruit body.
B: The fruit body is longer than the crown of leaves.
context: A pineapple is a tropical fruit with a leafy crown.
coding: Compare body length to crown length from their junction along the fruit axis. Exclude background leaves and use U if cropped, too close or indistinct.

A: Both large rear wheels are visible.
B: Only one large rear wheel is visible.
context: A wheelchair has a seat on wheels.
coding: Count distinct visible large rear wheels including a clear edge-on second wheel. Ignore the small casters and use U for an unresolved wheel.

A: The whole bird including its tail is visible.
B: Only part of the bird is visible and the tail is missing.
context: The parrot has a curved beak and a feathered body.
coding: Count intentional head-only drawings as B. Use U if a small overlapping object obscures whether the tail is present.

A: A clapper protrudes below the lower rim.
B: Nothing protrudes below the lower rim.
context: A bell is a hollow object with a flared opening.
coding: Count only a central hanging clapper or its attached stem. Use U where the rim or clapper is unresolvable.

A: The head is seen in side profile.
context: The camel has a long neck and a long muzzle.
coding: Use A for a clear lateral silhouette, B when muzzle faces the viewer with eyes or head sides roughly balanced, U for an intermediate angle.

A: A label is visibly marked on the body.
B: The body is plain with no visible label.
context: The wine bottle has a neck above a wider body.
coding: A label needs a distinct rectangular or bounded patch or obvious printed label; reflections alone do not qualify. Use U for cropped or occluded bodies.

A: The long object lies almost horizontally across the image.
B: The long object is steeply tilted in the image.
context: The rifle has a long narrow silhouette.
coding: Describe the image orientation only. Use A within roughly 15 degrees of horizontal and B beyond roughly 30 degrees. Intermediate is U.

A: The roof ends in a narrow pointed peak.
B: The roof has a broad top without a pointed peak.
context: The skyscraper is a tall building with many floors.
coding: A visible spire on the main tower qualifies as A; a broad stepped roof without a spire is B. U if its top is cut off.

B: The tail extends nearly horizontally behind the bird.
context: The songbird has a short beak and a feathered body.
coding: Use A for a tail descending more than roughly 35 degrees from horizontal, B within roughly 20 degrees of horizontal; use U for hidden, steeply upward or intermediate tails.

A: The two blade tips are spread apart.
B: The two blade tips are closed together.
context: The scissors have two handles joined at a pivot.
coding: Use A for a clear open gap between the two tips, B for touching or essentially aligned tips, U when occluded or indeterminate.

A: Two distinct horns are visible on the nose.
B: One horn is visible on the nose.
context: The rhinoceros has a heavy body and thick skin.
coding: Count nose horns only, not ears. Mark zero, occluded or ambiguous as U.

A: The tail lies higher in the image than the nose.
B: The nose lies higher in the image than the tail.
context: The dolphin has a streamlined body and fins.
coding: Compare the two ends of the same animal if clearly visible; U for level, hidden or indistinct ends.

A: An open frame spans above the narrow blade.
B: The broad solid blade has no frame above it.
context: The saw is a hand tool with a handle.
coding: An open bow or hacksaw frame is A, a clearly broad frameless plate is B, and a thin unsupported blade or indeterminate outline is U.

A: The top of the doorway is arched.
B: The top of the doorway is straight across.
context: The door is set in an opening in a wall.
coding: Use the upper door or opening boundary, not a small decorative panel within the door. U if the boundary is hidden or two conflict.

A: The wings are spread away from the body.
B: The wings are folded against the body.
context: The bat is a small mammal with membranous wings.
coding: Use A for visibly extended wings and B for folded wings. A head-only view or hidden wing posture is U.
